items.text:
Leo Kinyera

Biomedical Engineer | AI Systems Builder | MRI & Embedded Systems Researcher

Read the blog Resume CV

I design and build systems that operate beneath the surface—where signals, fields, and intelligence converge.

My work sits at the intersection of:

  • Medical imaging systems (MRI, RF, gradient design)
  • Artificial intelligence for signal reconstruction and interpretation
  • Embedded systems and edge intelligence (TinyML, microcontrollers)
  • Electronics and PCB design for high-performance applications

I am particularly interested in developing low-field MRI systems enhanced by AI, with the goal of making advanced medical imaging more accessible and scalable.

items.title: Philosophy
items.text:
Engineering, to me, is not about assembling components. It is about understanding the invisible forces that govern how systems behave—and designing with those forces in mind.

I approach problems from first principles, focusing on: - Signal behavior rather than abstraction - System interactions rather than isolated parts - Constraints as drivers of innovation

items.title: Selected Work & Research
items.text:
• AI models for enhancing low-field MRI image quality
  • Gradient system design and slice-select implementation
  • RF coil design and signal acquisition systems
  • Embedded AI systems on constrained hardware
  • Safety frameworks for MRI (PNS and SAR monitoring)

items.title: Closing Note
items.text:
I am currently focused on building systems that integrate physics, intelligence, and hardware into cohesive, real-world solutions.

If your work intersects with these domains—or aims to push the boundaries of medical and intelligent systems— I am always open to meaningful collaboration.

items.title: Engineering the Invisible: A Beginning
items.text:
This blog is an invitation to look beneath the surface of technology—to the interactions, fields, and signals that quietly govern how systems really work. Here you’ll find rigorous yet accessible explorations of MRI, AI, electronics, and embedded systems, approached from first principles rather than buzzwords.

Across these writings, I focus on building deep intuition, designing systems that sense, think, and act, and treating constraints as catalysts for better engineering. If you are willing to think carefully and question assumptions, this space will help you develop the mindset of a systems builder, not just a technology user.

Read my latest blog posts

The world, beneath its surfaces, is not made of objects. It is made of interactions.

I did not arrive in engineering through fascination with machines. I arrived through a question:

What is truly happening underneath?

Why does a wire carry meaning? How does a magnetic field become an image? How does a pattern of voltages become intelligence?

items.title: The Frontier I Am Exploring
items.text:
My work lives at the intersection of disciplines that rarely speak fluently to one another:

  • Medical imaging systems that turn physics into perception
  • Artificial intelligence that reconstructs and interprets reality
  • Electronics and PCB design where signals are shaped with intention
  • Embedded systems where intelligence meets constraint

Individually, these fields are powerful.

Together, they become something else entirely:

systems that sense, think, and act

items.title: What You Should Expect
items.text:
This is not a place for surface-level explanations.

We will: - Build intuition from first principles - Translate complex systems into clear mental models - Design—not just describe—engineering solutions - Examine failures as carefully as successes

Some posts will be simple.

Others will demand patience.

All of them will be honest.

items.title: Why This Matters
items.text:
We are entering an era where:

  • Machines will assist in diagnosis
  • Signals will define medical truth
  • Intelligence will be embedded into hardware

But these systems will only be as good as the engineers who build them.

And most systems today are built by people who: - follow instructions - replicate patterns - rarely question foundations

This must change.

items.title: A Different Approach
items.text:
I am not interested in being a user of technology.

I am interested in becoming a builder of systems that others rely on.

That requires a different mindset:

  • To see circuits as fields, not just connections
  • To see MRI as signal processing, not just imaging
  • To see AI as a tool, not magic
  • To see constraints as design opportunities

items.title: What Comes Next
items.text:
In the coming writings, we will explore:

  • Why MRI is fundamentally a signal processing problem
  • How gradient coils actually shape space
  • What it takes to design RF systems from scratch
  • Whether AI can truly elevate low-field imaging
  • How to embed intelligence into constrained hardware

Not as isolated topics—

but as parts of a single, evolving system.

items.title: Final Note
items.text:
If you are looking for quick answers, this may not be the place.

But if you are willing to think—deeply, rigorously, patiently—

then you will begin to see what most overlook:

that engineering is not about components

it is about understanding the invisible forces that shape reality

This is only the beginning.

And we are going all the way down.
